title: 2 Samuel Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 7.

questions.question: What had the LORD given King David before he sat in his house?
options: Rest round about from all his enemies
A new palace
A great army
A harvest of abundance
questions.correctAnswer: Rest round about from all his enemies
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:1 states that the LORD had given David rest round about from all his enemies before he sat in his house.

questions.question: To whom did King David speak about dwelling in a house of cedar while the ark of God dwelt within curtains?
options: Nathan the prophet
Samuel the prophet
Gad the seer
Joab the commander
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan the prophet
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 7:2, David said unto Nathan the prophet about his dwelling in a house of cedar and the ark dwelling within curtains.

questions.question: What was Nathan's initial response to King David about doing what was in his heart?
options: Go, do all that is in thine heart; for the LORD is with thee.
Wait for the LORD's command.
Seek counsel from the elders first.
Build a tabernacle instead.
questions.correctAnswer: Go, do all that is in thine heart; for the LORD is with thee.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:3 records Nathan telling David to do all that is in his heart because the LORD is with him.

questions.question: What happened to Nathan that night after speaking with King David?
options: The word of the LORD came unto Nathan
He had a dream about the ark
He met the elders of Israel
He was commanded to build a house
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto Nathan
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:4 states that that night the word of the LORD came unto Nathan.

questions.question: What question did the LORD ask Nathan to tell David?
options: Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?
Will you lead Israel to victory?
Shall the ark remain in the tabernacle?
Will your kingdom last forever?
questions.correctAnswer: Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:5 records that the LORD asked Nathan to tell David if he should build Him a house to dwell in.

questions.question: Since when had the LORD not dwelt in any house?
options: Since the time He brought up Israel out of Egypt
Since the time of Moses' death
Since the conquest of Canaan
Since the days of Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: Since the time He brought up Israel out of Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:6 explains that the LORD had not dwelt in any house from the time he brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt.

questions.question: How had the LORD moved among the children of Israel instead of dwelling in a house?
options: In a tent and in a tabernacle
In a palace
In a mountain cave
In the temple
questions.correctAnswer: In a tent and in a tabernacle
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:6 states that the LORD walked in a tent and in a tabernacle among the children of Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He never commanded any of the tribes of Israel to do?
options: To build Him a house of cedar
To offer sacrifices daily
To appoint kings over them
To fight their neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: To build Him a house of cedar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:7 records that the LORD never commanded the tribes of Israel to build Him a house of cedar.

questions.question: From what did the LORD take David to make him ruler over Israel?
options: From the sheepcote, from following the sheep
From the fields of wheat
From the city gates
From the priests
questions.correctAnswer: From the sheepcote, from following the sheep
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:8 states that the LORD took David from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He had done for David wherever he went?
options: Cut off all his enemies and made him a great name
Given him many wives
Made him wealthy beyond measure
Given him many sons
questions.correctAnswer: Cut off all his enemies and made him a great name
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:9 says the LORD was with David and cut off all his enemies, making him a great name.

questions.question: What will the LORD appoint for the people of Israel according to His promise to David?
options: A place to dwell in and not be moved
A new temple in Jerusalem
A new law for judges
A mighty army
questions.correctAnswer: A place to dwell in and not be moved
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:10 states that the LORD will appoint a place for Israel to dwell in and not be moved.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan told David to immediately build a house for the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:5-7 shows that the LORD questioned whether David should build Him a house and explained that He had not asked anyone to do so before.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised David that his kingdom and house would be established forever.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:16 declares that David’s house and kingdom shall be established forever.

questions.question: True or False: David prayed a prayer of humility and praise after hearing Nathan's message.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:18-29 records David’s prayer expressing humility and praise before the LORD.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 7, which event comes first?
options: David speaks to Nathan about the house of cedar
The LORD gives Nathan a vision
Nathan tells David to build a house
David prays before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: David speaks to Nathan about the house of cedar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:2 shows David first speaking to Nathan about his house of cedar before the LORD gives Nathan a vision (verse 4).

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What promise does God make to David concerning his descendants in 2 Samuel 7?
options: David's descendants will build a temple and have an everlasting kingdom
David's descendants will be kings for only a few generations
David will have no descendants to rule after him
David's descendants will be priests instead of kings
questions.correctAnswer: David's descendants will build a temple and have an everlasting kingdom
questions.explanation: God promises in 2 Samuel 7:12-13 that David's seed will establish a kingdom and build a house for God's name, with a throne established forever.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 7:14 describe the relationship between God and David's descendant?
options: God will be his father, and he will be God's son
They will be distant and not communicate
God will punish him without mercy
He will be equal to God
questions.correctAnswer: God will be his father, and he will be God's son
questions.explanation: Verse 14 clearly states God will be the father and the descendant will be His son, indicating a special, intimate relationship.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7:15, what is said about God's mercy toward David's descendant compared to Saul?
options: God's mercy will not depart from David's descendant as it did from Saul
God will withdraw mercy from David's descendant like Saul
God will never show mercy to any king
God will treat Saul and David's descendant the same
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy will not depart from David's descendant as it did from Saul
questions.explanation: Verse 15 contrasts the mercy shown to Saul with the enduring mercy that will remain with David's descendant.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 7:16 say about the stability of David's house and kingdom?
options: They shall be established forever and the throne shall be established forever
They will last only a few years
They will be destroyed after David's death
They will be shared with other kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be established forever and the throne shall be established forever
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly declares the eternal establishment of David's house, kingdom, and throne.

questions.question: How did Nathan respond to David after receiving God's message in 2 Samuel 7:17?
options: He spoke all the words and vision exactly as the Lord commanded
He refused to deliver the message
He altered the message to suit David
He told David to ignore the vision
questions.correctAnswer: He spoke all the words and vision exactly as the Lord commanded
questions.explanation: Verse 17 confirms Nathan faithfully relayed God's message and vision to David.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 7:18, how does David express his feelings before the LORD after hearing the prophecy?
options: David humbly questions his worthiness and the significance of his house
David arrogantly claims he deserves the blessing
David ignores the prophecy
David demands more promises
questions.correctAnswer: David humbly questions his worthiness and the significance of his house
questions.explanation: David asks, 'Who am I... and what is my house,' showing humility and awe (verse 18).

questions.question: What does David acknowledge about the promise concerning his house in 2 Samuel 7:19?
options: It is a small thing compared to what God has planned for the future
It is a trivial promise with no real importance
It only concerns David's lifetime
It was a common promise made to all kings
questions.correctAnswer: It is a small thing compared to what God has planned for the future
questions.explanation: David reflects that the promise is small in God's sight but extends far into the future (verse 19).

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7:20, why does David feel he cannot say more to the LORD?
options: Because the LORD knows his servant thoroughly
Because David is angry and silent
Because he is uncertain about God's plan
Because he does not trust God
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD knows his servant thoroughly
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God's intimate knowledge of him, making further words unnecessary (verse 20).

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 7:11 connect the establishment of David's house to his rest from enemies?
options: Since God caused David to rest from enemies, He will also make him a house
David’s rest from enemies is unrelated to the promise of a house
David must fight more battles before getting a house
The house will be destroyed by enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Since God caused David to rest from enemies, He will also make him a house
questions.explanation: Verse 11 links David's peace from foes to God's promise to build him a lasting house.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 7:12 promise will happen after David’s days are fulfilled?
options: God will set up David's seed to succeed him and establish his kingdom
David’s kingdom will end with him
David will be forgotten
His descendants will be exiled
questions.correctAnswer: God will set up David's seed to succeed him and establish his kingdom
questions.explanation: Verse 12 promises the succession of David’s lineage and kingdom continuation.

questions.question: What lesson about humility can believers learn from David’s response in 2 Samuel 7:18-20?
options: To recognize God’s greatness and our own unworthiness before His promises
To demand more blessings from God
To rely on our own strength for success
To ignore God’s plans
questions.correctAnswer: To recognize God’s greatness and our own unworthiness before His promises
questions.explanation: David’s humble questioning and acknowledgment of God’s knowledge (verses 18-20) teach believers to trust and submit to God’s will.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 7:13-14 teach about God's discipline and mercy in leadership?
options: God will discipline iniquity but His mercy will endure
God never disciplines leaders
Leaders are punished without mercy
Discipline means removal from leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God will discipline iniquity but His mercy will endure
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show God’s fatherly discipline balanced with enduring mercy for the king’s line.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 7:16, David’s throne would be established only for his lifetime.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states David’s throne shall be established forever, not limited to his lifetime.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 7:20 indicates David felt fully understood by God and had nothing more to say.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God's intimate knowledge of him, indicating he felt no need to say more (verse 20).

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 7:19, David believed the promise about his house was insignificant in God's sight.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David said the promise was a small thing in his own eyes but not in God's sight, indicating it was significant (verse 19).

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7, what reason does God give for not needing a house to dwell in?
options: He prefers to dwell in the hearts of His people
He has not dwelt in any house since bringing Israel from Egypt, but walked in a tent and tabernacle
He is invisible and cannot be contained
He dwells only in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: He has not dwelt in any house since bringing Israel from Egypt, but walked in a tent and tabernacle
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:6 states that the LORD has not dwelt in any house since the Exodus but has walked in a tent and tabernacle.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' in 2 Samuel 7:14?
options: It foreshadows the Davidic covenant and messianic promise
It refers to Solomon's role as temple builder
It describes the relationship between Nathan and David
It indicates the adoption of Israel as God's children
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Davidic covenant and messianic promise
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:14 uses father-son imagery to establish the covenantal relationship that foreshadows the messianic promise fulfilled in the New Testament, such as Hebrews 1:5.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 7:23, how does David describe the nation of Israel in comparison to other nations?
options: As a nation like any other
As a chosen people redeemed by God from Egypt and other nations
As a nation without a God
As a nation conquered by other gods
questions.correctAnswer: As a chosen people redeemed by God from Egypt and other nations
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:23 emphasizes Israel's uniqueness because God redeemed them from Egypt and from other nations and gods, making them His chosen people.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Samuel 7:27-29 in David's prayer?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: David's prayer in 2 Samuel 7:27-29 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, by repeating ideas about God's promises and blessings in a balanced structure.

questions.question: What does David acknowledge about God in 2 Samuel 7:22?
options: That God is one among many gods
That God is great and there is none like Him
That God sometimes makes mistakes
That God is distant and unknowable
questions.correctAnswer: That God is great and there is none like Him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:22 declares God's greatness and uniqueness, stating there is none like Him and no other God besides Him.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'bayit' (house) in 2 Samuel 7 most directly refer to in the context of God's promise to David?
options: A physical temple building
David’s descendants and dynasty
The city of Jerusalem
The tabernacle curtains
questions.correctAnswer: David’s descendants and dynasty
questions.explanation: 'Bayit' in 2 Samuel 7 often symbolizes not just a physical house but the dynasty or lineage of David, emphasizing the covenantal promise of an enduring royal line (2 Samuel 7:12-16).

questions.question: What is the historical and cultural significance of God telling David He took him 'from following the sheep' in 2 Samuel 7:8?
options: It shows David's humble origins as a shepherd boy before becoming king
It means David was a shepherd of religious ceremonies
It implies David was a shepherd for the temple priests
It symbolizes David's role as a farmer
questions.correctAnswer: It shows David's humble origins as a shepherd boy before becoming king
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:8 references David’s humble beginnings as a shepherd, a common metaphor for leadership and care, before his divine appointment as king.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7:25, what does David request God to do concerning His word about David and his house?
options: Forget the promise
Establish it forever and do as He has said
Delay the promise
Make it conditional on David's continued obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Establish it forever and do as He has said
questions.explanation: David prays in 2 Samuel 7:25 for God to firmly establish His spoken promise about David and his house forever, asking for fulfillment as declared.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the promise of an everlasting throne made to David in 2 Samuel 7:16?
options: Romans 3:23
Hebrews 11:1
James 2:17
questions.explanation: Acts 2:29-30 references God's promise to David of an everlasting throne, connecting the Davidic covenant in 2 Samuel 7:16 with the messianic hope fulfilled in Jesus.

questions.question: What does David mean when he says, 'Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?' in 2 Samuel 7:18?
options: He expresses humility and amazement at God's blessings
He questions God's authority
He complains about his hardships
He demands a sign from God
questions.correctAnswer: He expresses humility and amazement at God's blessings
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 7:18, David humbly acknowledges his lowly status and marvels at how God has brought him to this point, showing his gratitude and reverence.

questions.question: What is the theme of God's mercy in relation to David's house as contrasted with Saul's in 2 Samuel 7?
options: God's mercy will depart from David's house as it did from Saul's
God's mercy remains with David's house unlike with Saul's
God shows no mercy to either house
God favors Saul's house over David's
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy remains with David's house unlike with Saul's
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:15 highlights that God's mercy will not depart from David's house as it did from Saul's, emphasizing the enduring covenant with David.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage contains a similar promise about the eternal reign of David's offspring?
options: Psalm 89:3-4
Genesis 12:1-3
Exodus 20:1-17
Leviticus 19:18
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 89:3-4
questions.explanation: Psalm 89:3-4 echoes the promise of an eternal dynasty for David's line, reinforcing the covenant theme found in 2 Samuel 7.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 7:21, why does David say God has done great things to make him know them?
options: Because David is a prophet
For God's word's sake and according to His own heart
Because David was a great warrior
Because of David's wealth
questions.correctAnswer: For God's word's sake and according to His own heart
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:21 explains that God performed great deeds for David to know them, motivated by His word and heart, emphasizing divine initiative.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Samuel 7:29, David asks God to bless his house so it may continue forever before Him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:29 records David's prayer asking God to bless his house so it may continue forever before Him.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 7 states that Nathan immediately disobeyed God's instruction and told David to build the temple at once.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 7:4-5, God instructs Nathan to tell David not to build the house, but Nathan initially encouraged David before receiving God's word, so he did not disobey God's instruction.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give in 2 Samuel 7 for not dwelling in a house since bringing Israel out of Egypt?
options: He preferred to dwell in tents and tabernacles
He was displeased with Israel's idolatry
He was preparing a temple for Solomon
He was punishing Israel for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: He preferred to dwell in tents and tabernacles
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:6 explains that God has not dwelt in a house since bringing Israel out of Egypt, but instead has walked in a tent and tabernacle, showing His preference for a mobile dwelling during that period.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7, what was God's initial response to David's desire to build a house for the ark?
options: God questioned whether David should build Him a house
God immediately approved the building of the temple
God instructed David to build a larger tabernacle
God told David to wait until Solomon's reign
questions.correctAnswer: God questioned whether David should build Him a house
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:5 records God's word to Nathan asking if David should build a house for God to dwell in, indicating a divine questioning rather than immediate approval.

questions.question: Which doctrine is primarily taught by God's promise to 'establish the throne of his kingdom forever' through David's seed, as seen in 2 Samuel 7:13?
options: The doctrine of the Davidic Covenant
The doctrine of justification by faith
The doctrine of original sin
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the Davidic Covenant
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:13 presents God's promise to establish the kingdom of David's seed forever, which is foundational to the doctrine of the Davidic Covenant, a key promise of eternal kingship.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in 2 Samuel 7:15 where God says, 'But my mercy shall not depart away from him'?
options: God's mercy and faithfulness
God's wrath and justice
God's omnipresence
God's sovereignty over nature
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and faithfulness
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 7:15, God's declaration that His mercy will not depart from David's lineage shows His enduring mercy and faithfulness, distinguishing His covenantal love from His treatment of Saul.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 7:8 describe God's intervention in David's life?
options: God took David from tending sheep to rule over Israel
God gave David a large army to defeat his enemies
God gifted David with prophetic abilities
God appointed David as a priest
questions.correctAnswer: God took David from tending sheep to rule over Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states that God took David from following sheep to be ruler over Israel, emphasizing divine calling and providence in David's rise.

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Samuel 7:11 and 2 Samuel 7:16 convey about the nature of God's kingdom and covenant with David?
options: God promises a perpetual kingdom and an eternal throne for David's house
God demands continual sacrifices to maintain David's kingdom
God's covenant with David is conditional on Israel's obedience
God's kingdom will be temporary and limited to David's lifetime
questions.correctAnswer: God promises a perpetual kingdom and an eternal throne for David's house
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:11 and 7:16 together affirm God's promise to establish David's house and kingdom forever, indicating an eternal, unbroken covenant.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's providence is revealed by 2 Samuel 7:9 where God says, 'I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest'?
options: God's constant presence and guidance in David's life
God's selective intervention only in battles
God's absence during David's early years
God's indifference to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God's constant presence and guidance in David's life
questions.explanation: Verse 9 emphasizes God's continual presence with David, reflecting the doctrine of divine providence overseeing and guiding believers.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 7:14, how does God relate to the future king who will build His house, and what is His response to iniquity?
options: God is a father to the king and will chasten him with men’s rods if he sins
God will abandon the king if he commits iniquity
God will immediately destroy the king for any sin
God will ignore the king's iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: God is a father to the king and will chasten him with men’s rods if he sins
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:14 reveals a father-son relationship between God and the king, with divine discipline administered as a father corrects a son, showing God's holiness and justice balanced with mercy.

questions.question: What does David’s prayer in 2 Samuel 7:18-20 reveal about his understanding of God's sovereignty and grace?
options: David acknowledges his lowliness and God's sovereign favor
David demands a larger kingdom
David questions God's promises
David focuses on military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: David acknowledges his lowliness and God's sovereign favor
questions.explanation: In verses 18-20, David humbly recognizes his insignificance and God's gracious acts, demonstrating an understanding of God's sovereign election and grace.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the promise of an eternal throne in 2 Samuel 7 is merely political and not divine. What does 2 Samuel 7:12-13 actually teach about the nature of this promise?
options: It is a divine promise of an everlasting kingdom through David's seed, foreshadowing Christ
It is a temporary political alliance with neighboring nations
It is conditional on Israel’s military strength alone
It refers only to Solomon’s reign
questions.correctAnswer: It is a divine promise of an everlasting kingdom through David's seed, foreshadowing Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 indicate that God will establish an eternal kingdom through David's offspring, a promise fulfilled ultimately in Christ, underscoring its divine and messianic nature beyond mere politics.

questions.question: Which combined doctrine is illustrated by the promise in 2 Samuel 7:25-26 about God's word and the establishment of David's house?
options: The doctrine of divine faithfulness and covenantal promise
The doctrine of angelic mediation
The doctrine of human merit in salvation
The doctrine of predestination without promise
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine faithfulness and covenantal promise
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 show David’s plea for God to fulfill His word, affirming God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises, a key biblical doctrine.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 7:23 emphasize about Israel’s uniqueness among nations?
options: Israel is uniquely redeemed and established by God from Egypt for His own name
Israel is one nation among many with no special status
Israel is rejected for their idolatry
Israel’s gods are superior to other nations’ gods
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is uniquely redeemed and established by God from Egypt for His own name
questions.explanation: Verse 23 declares Israel as uniquely chosen and redeemed by God from Egypt, highlighting their special relationship and mission, a foundational biblical theme.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining 2 Samuel 7:4 and 2 Samuel 7:27 about God's communication and revelation to David?
options: God reveals His covenant plans through prophets and directly to His servants
God only speaks through angels
God’s plans are hidden and never revealed
God communicates only to kings without prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His covenant plans through prophets and directly to His servants
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows God speaking to Nathan the prophet, and verse 27 shows God revealing His promise to David, illustrating divine communication through human agents and personal revelation.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 7:10 contribute to the biblical narrative of salvation history regarding Israel’s future?
options: It promises Israel permanent settlement free from oppression
It predicts Israel's exile and destruction
It foretells Israel’s rejection by God
It commands Israel to conquer new nations
questions.correctAnswer: It promises Israel permanent settlement free from oppression
questions.explanation: Verse 10 promises God will plant Israel so they will dwell securely without oppression, aligning with the biblical theme of covenantal blessing and restoration.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in 2 Samuel 7:22 where David declares, 'there is none like thee'?
options: God’s uniqueness and incomparable greatness
God’s invisibility
God’s limitation in power
God’s indifference to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s uniqueness and incomparable greatness
questions.explanation: Verse 22 shows David’s affirmation of God’s singular greatness and uniqueness, emphasizing the monotheistic claim of the Bible.
